utterances.text: These guards who beat you, were they at any point in time punished by the camp commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they were rewarded by the warden, because when the warden told me that nobody would beat me again, I really made a big mistake for having complained, because immediately I was beaten by three men with the comment, "so you are the one who complained about being beaten", so that I believed that the warden actually rewarded the ones who beat, because had they been punished, they would not have beaten people. In my view, the warden could not give the keys to those who came to beat balijas, the cells need not have been opened, but it was -- anybody could beat me, except when Dragan Micic was on duty. On several occasions he saved me from being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You were detained -- until when were you detained in Kaonik, Mr. Dautovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 19th June when I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: That was the year 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1993, yes. I learned that in Zenica in the hospital, it was there that I learned the date. I do not know what day it was to this day. I know the date, because I did not go home, I went to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Before you went to the hospital -- how did the release from the camp take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The release took place one morning, they said there would be an exchange today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Who said that to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Someone, one of the guards said that there would be an exchange. I do not know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Then what happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told, "but don't you expect to get out alive", this was through the keyhole, so I did not expect at all to get out of the camp. When they started reading out the names and I saw my wife, my child, my house, my family in my imagination, I thought what they looked like, because I considered myself dead. I was very envious of the people who were leaving, I thought they were the happiest people on earth. They read out those names and I heard my name and I banged on the door, I said, "I am Hamdo Dautovic, it is me, I am Dautovic", and then the cell was opened and the first thing that happened was a blow, "what are you shouting for?". Then I was taken in front of this woman from the International Red Cross, I said, "I am Dautovic Hamdo", so I stayed there in the corridor, among these people who were being released. I did not dare say hello to any one of them, because I did not believe it was possible that I would leave the place alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said you were brought to the lady who was -- a lady from the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not brought to her, I went there alone. From the cell to where she was, it was maybe five, six metres, I do not know exactly. It was in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were there others present with the lady on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were others, yes. I was the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How many -- when I meant others, were there other officials of the camp who were present on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you recall who they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall seeing the warden and a couple of others, but I do not know their names, because for me, whoever was in uniform and who was there was a camp official, or whether they came to visit or on purpose to beat balijas, because everyone had the right to do that, so they were all the same to me, because I was the one who suffered their blows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: By warden you mean Zlatko Aleksovski the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean Zlatko, yes, because there was no other warden. I knew of no other guard except Zlatko while I was there, because I could not kiss his feet and if that would have helped, I would have done that, but I probably would have been kicked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Together with you, how many others were released on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I was the 39th, because when I was getting into the bus, I looked at a woman who was reading out the name and my name was written differently from the others. The other names were typed by typewriter, my name was written by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were you able to observe the reaction of the guards when you were released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Terrible, terrible. Goran Medugorac was coming in from some place, he was carrying some bags and when I saw him and when he saw me, I thought he would kill me, because he was the one who said I would not leave alive. The window was open, and I heard him enter the warden's office and say to him, "did you not promise me that Dautovic would not leave alive?". I then acted being even more sick than I was, but I heard Zlatko say to him, "you see he is going to die anyway, so it is better that he die in their custody than in ours".

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Then you said together with the other 38 you got into a van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said you got into -- you were released from custody, your name was the 39th on the list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You overheard this conversation between the guard Medugorac and Zlatko the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where were you when you heard this conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was close by, the window was open, I was right in front, because there is a narrow path in front of the entrance and the office was left of the entrance, it was the first office to the left, that was the office of the warden. Because that was when I was so frightened, because I had some hopes of surviving and then I saw Goran Medugorac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: So despite the conversation, you were released from custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was already outside among the others, among the other 38 who were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where were you taken to from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told that we should go to the gate, to the bus. I gained some strength, but as I tried to walk, I fell. Then two men who had also been released from the prison almost carried me to the bus between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: So in the bus, where were you transported to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Then you spent a day in the Zenica hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were you treated at the Zenica hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent the night there, I was examined by a doctor, she said that I had been beaten badly, "your kidneys are probably badly damaged". The neuropsychiatrist also examined me and I had to see the neuropsychiatrist for two years and she helped me a lot, she gave me a lot of advice, telling me how to behave, to walk along the river, how to regain some sort of normality, so that I went to see a neuropsychiatrist for two years. Then I had an ultrasound examination of all my internal organs and I have the findings on me, they said that the kidneys were damaged, but not my other internal organs so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you still suffer as a result of the consequences of your stay in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have bad consequences. I feel very tired, and I feel sleepy, but I cannot fall asleep. Then I cannot memorise things, sometimes I talk to myself, I feel I am forgetful, because I remember well what happened to me ten years ago, but what happened to me now, a couple of days back, I cannot remember. A face of a person I met before the war I still remember that person, if I meet him, but I am somehow ashamed, I sometimes am introduced to the same persons in five days twice. I feel a certain amount of mental disorder. I am not an idiot, far from that. If I have a small glass of alcohol, every two minutes I have to go to the toilet, so I avoid alcohol for that reason, mostly, not that I would not like a drink, but that is the consequence that I have. Then I get angry all of a sudden, I have become terribly tense so that I can explode briefly, but there is no cure for that, so I am trying to be alone and trying to be patient about it, but it is very difficult. A couple of times I went by car to Zenica, I left the car, went to a cafe bar, had a drink, found some friends, talked to them for a while; after that I do not know where I left the car, and I did not know what to do. If I went to the police and told them that they had stolen my car, I knew it was not true and I was ashamed to tell my friends of the same thing and then after about an hour and a half I found my car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you still take medication for your illnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. It is a sad thing to say, but I go to the doctors often. A change of weather and I fall sick, a bit of strain or something unpleasant happens to me, I get insomnia and very dark thoughts, so I find it difficult to orientate myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Before going into detention, before you were arrested and detained in the camp, what was your physical condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not as heavy as I am now, I was more of a sporty type, I was very healthy, very fit, very, very fit, so I thought nobody could do anything to me, that I could never fall ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you suffer from insomnia before being detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: As far as you know, did you have any bad or damaged kidneys before you were detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before my detention, I was never ill, I worked in a mine for eight years. I was working in the pit and I never went to see a doctor. Then for several years I was a caterer and again I never went to see a doctor. In fact I found it strange when somebody asked me about doctors, because I did not know any doctors. It was only my late mother that would go to see a doctor and that is how I came to know of some doctors, through her, but otherwise I never went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: That is all, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mikulicic, can we start with a cross-examination before lunch or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In view of the time, the Defence would suggest that we have a lunch break and then that we have the cross-examination without interruption after the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well. Are you agreeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In that case, we are going to have a lunch break and we will resume work at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. We are going to resume the hearing by giving the floor to Mr. Mikulicic for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Good afternoon, Mr. Dautovic, I am attorney Mr. Goran Mikulicic, Defence counsel for Mr. Zlatko Aleksovski in this Trial Chamber. I have a few questions for you and will you please answer them to the best of your recollection, so that we may establish the factual truth. Mr. Dautovic, you said you were born in Han Bila, or rather that you lived in Han Bila?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Maline, but I am living close to Han Bila. These are all villages close to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Where did you go to elementary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You completed eight years of elementary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you have any further education, will you tell us what school you attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I passed my seventh and eighth grade through evening classes, I passed an examination for a qualified driver, and then through evening classes, I went through commercial school and mining school, so that I am a skilled miner as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: These commercial and mining schools, how long did they last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I attended those schools part-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you explain that? Is it a kind of course or regular education, or does it involve just passing examinations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just examinations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And what qualifications did you acquire after completing those schools?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the area of commerce I became a qualified trader, and as a miner, I was employed in a mine and for a driver, I passed that test in Dito Verbas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What were the jobs that you held after your education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked as a miner, I worked near Kruscica as a salesman, I never worked as a driver, though I do have a licence, and now I have a private cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You told us that you had a cafe bar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I still do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: For how long have you had that coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, does it have a name, this coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does, it is called "Sreca", or "Luck".

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And this coffee bar is in Han Bila?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Dautovic, working in catering, did you have any unpleasantness, any disorders in your coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That happens in any catering institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you have any dealings with the local police in that connection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Any caterer, if there is any disturbance, is obliged to report it to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us, Mr. Dautovic, who were the people who frequented your bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a difficult question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I did not mean you to name them. If you could just describe them as to where they came from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you are asking. All kinds of people came to my coffee bar, not just people of one particular circle, with various educations, of all ethnic backgrounds, Serbs, Croats, Muslims, so there was -- I am a hospitable person and everyone is welcome who is a good guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, were you prominent in any political activities in your environment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Are you a member of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Since when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were three parties, who else would I be for?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am not asking you why, I am asking you from when.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From when it was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you have any position in the party, or were you just a member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no function.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Dautovic, did you personally have any conflicts with the law? Were you ever charged or punished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally was punished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because of fights, disturbance of the public law and order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who were the people you had any conflicts with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was usually under the influence of alcohol with my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will go back to 18th May 1993, the date you said you remembered well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You have told us in outline what happened on that day. What we are interested in, in addition to what you have said, is what was the reason for your journey that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To buy cigarettes in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you buy the cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two and a half boxes, that is 100 and something boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many boxes are there in one carton?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And how many packs in one box?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Where, in what shop did you buy those cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not buy them in a shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Who did you buy the cigarettes from if you did not buy them in a shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I bought them from a guy in Guca Gora, I do not know his name. I know him well, we went to school together, but he is much younger than me. It is in the direction of the school, from the church, a house south of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How come that man had cigarettes when he did not have a shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time the difference in prices was considerable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, he did not tell me how he got the cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am asking you for the differences in prices.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The profits were considerable and I wanted to make a profit so I wanted to get them as cheaply as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Will you please correct me if I am wrong: can it be said that the cigarettes that you bought were not bought legally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I bought them illegally. I did not buy them legally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that you were in a car with Mr. Mujo Beganovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with Mujo Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that you were stopped by Ivica Bobas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What uniform did he have on that occasion? You said he was in an uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps notice the colour of his belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: White belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What did that mean, if somebody was wearing a uniform with a white belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he was a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, when you said that you were stopped by Ivica Bobas, is it correct for me to assume that you knew him well from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was he a person who came to your coffee bar as a neighbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Ivica Bobas has a brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His name -- one brother's name was Kazimir, who worked with me in the mine. I think the oldest one is called Pero, because he is ill, and then he has another brother, and I do not know all their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Of course it is only normal that you cannot remember them all. Mr. Dautovic, did you ever have any conflicts with the brother of Ivica Bobas, Pero Bobas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, do you know somebody called Kasimovic, known as Koro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, he was my neighbour -- he is now my neighbour. He was not before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I remember well, you said that Ivica Bobas, on that occasion, was soon joined by three other persons in uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did they have white belts as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two of them did, but the one who had a pistol -- two of them had rifles, but as for the one who had a pistol, I do not remember whether he had a white belt or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Who ordered you to get out of the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivica Bobas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said regarding Mujo, Mujo Beganovic who was with you, that he was allowed to go home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did, he went home straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was he explicitly told that he could go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was clearly told, "you are free and you may go", and he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, how did you interpret this behaviour? They stopped you, however they let the person who was with you in the car go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never managed to find any explanation for that. I do not know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did these military police men ask you who owned the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What did you answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told them it was mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did they search your car on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not, but Ivica Bobas ordered me to empty my pockets and put what I had on the car. I had another 17,000 German marks and some change, I do not remember how much, and I had the keys of the car. I put all that on the hood. My car was turned on and driven away. I never saw it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, how much did you pay for those two and a half cartons of cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember, they were expensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Not even roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly about 2,000 or 2,500, but I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You are talking about German marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, everything was in German marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, can you remember in those days, that is in May 1993, what was roughly the average salary in Travnik, Han Bila and Central Bosnia in those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us roughly at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not employed, so I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What were your daily or monthly earnings in your coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That depended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us with some more precision?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, we did not hear the witness. Could the witness repeat the answer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: (Not interpreted).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One needed to have 400 to 500 Deutschmarks. If I had found enough cigarettes, I would have spent all my money on cigarettes and that is why I took everything with me that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interrupt, I think some questions and answers did not go down on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: There was an answer that was not translated. Could you please repeat the question, Mr. Mikulicic, and the witness's answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The question addressed to Mr. Dautovic was whether he could tell us with greater precision how much he paid for the cigarettes, or how much roughly was the monthly earnings of his coffee bar. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I think that was the question that was asked but was not translated, and then the question which followed that was also not translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I shall try in the future to slow down a little bit so as to give enough time to the interpreters. So Mr. Dautovic, because the interpreters did not manage to interpret our conversation as we are speaking in languages that are very close to one another. I am going to repeat my question. Can you specify how much your coffee bar earned in 1993, in that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think that you said sometimes you covered costs and sometimes you did not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What were your monthly expenditures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, is it not rather strange for a businessman not to know his earnings or his expenditures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to this event, this incident. If I understood you well, you set off with about 20,000 German marks. You think you will facilitate the interpreter's job? My question was, why did you take so much money with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because that was how much I had. It was a short trip, it was only a couple of kilometres that I traversed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So you put your money and other personal belongings on the hood of the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, on the roof of the car, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And after that the money was taken away from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not taken away, I left it on the roof of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What happened with that money later? Was it returned to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was divided up among the four people in my presence. I do not know whether it was shared out equally, but I know that each one of them took some money from the stack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that, you headed towards the police station in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With them, because I was ordered to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that, you boarded a car, make Fiat Ritmo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many doors does that car have, that model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recollect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you notice the licence plates on the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew the car, because it belonged to Edhem Lukovic, from Han Bila, which was confiscated a couple of days before that in Guca Gora too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Dautovic, that you sat in the back, in the middle, between two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two soldiers. I was just going to correct myself and to say that the car had four doors, two in front, two in the back, and that I think it was a grey colour or something like that, but I do not really know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you recollect how much you weighed at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, but over 90, between 90 and 100 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Along what road did you go from Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Radojcici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At Radojcici was there a BiH army checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just above Radojcici, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was the car stopped at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not. I had to bend my head down between my knees so there were two people sitting behind, not three, because people could see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, the car passed through the BiH army checkpoint without stopping. Was that natural?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had the courage at the time to go to the Croatian sections, because I had nothing to fear, I had not done anything, so nobody feared the Croats if they had not done anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But that is not my question. Was it normal for cars not to be stopped at checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it was not suspicious, there was no need for cars to be stopped. I crossed all the checkpoints, both Croatian and Muslim and rarely was I stopped in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you not say a moment ago that the car was stolen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Does that fact not show that it was a suspicious car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not suspicious, because Edhem Lukovic was the real owner, an elderly man, he had died and they confiscated the car from him. He was a tax collector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Very well. As you drove on, you said that you tried to escape from the car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that you pushed the person sitting on your left, so that he fell out the door, together with you, from the car. Mr. Dautovic, you are a qualified driver. Could you assess the speed at which the car was going when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twenty, thirty, it was very slow, because it is not -- it was not an asphalt road but a macadam road, it was going very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you explain and describe how you fell out of the car, on to what kind of ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I hit the person, the driver skidded off the road and so did the car, so it was into a meadow that we fell, because the car went right off the road then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Dautovic, but I cannot understand that. Did the car go off the road after you fell out, or did you fall out after the car had driven off the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: With what part of the body did you hit the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What part of the body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This side here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Please tell us for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Were you hurt on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, you said that at that time you wanted to grab the rifle. Of whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the soldier who was to the left of me, that is why I tried to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Why did you want to take the rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In order to kill them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Why would you want to kill them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where were they taking me? They were taking me to kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that they would kill you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At what point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several times, because several times I was hit by the knife handle in the neck area and with the rifle butt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In other words during the ride?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us how you wanted to take the rifle away from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us try to clarify the question. This is the situation. You are tumbling out of the car which is moving, together with another car. Three persons remain in the car which is veering off the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The three of them came out right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: From whom are you trying to grab the rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the man with whom I tumbled out, but I immediately got a barrel into my mouth and I surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, in the events that you just described, can you specify, with respect to the point where you tumbled out of the car, where did the vehicle out of which you tumbled out stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right there, there was just a shoulder a metre away off the road and that is where it stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that, you said that another car arrived.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At that time, they did not put you in the vehicle but in the boot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that, how long did you ride in this car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, it was too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Then you came where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of a building where there was light, and the boot was opened and they said, "we have a balija extremist for you", and an unknown voice said, "he is not for us, it is Hamdo, take him away somewhere else".

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that, you arrived where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, I was driven and I heard from the boot that they were going to kill me, that they would let me go and then they would kill me while trying to escape, but I did not know where. I did not know where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When did you finally get an opportunity to get out of the vehicle? Where were you then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, somewhere in some woods, it was a small wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said, "you have a child, you are a good man", then I knew they would shoot at me when I came out, so I pretended to be even more hurt than I was so that I would not have to come out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, what I am trying to ask of you, and I do not seem to be succeeding, at least I am not succeeding in getting the answer of you, is when you ultimately -- when was it that you ultimately arrived to a facility that you arrived at? Did you know what facility it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Micic Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you know Dragan Micic from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Who was Dragan Micic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A soldier, a guard in the prison, I do not know. I know that he was there in the prison and that he did not beat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How did you conclude that he was a guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he unlocked my cell a couple of times, he gave me water a couple of times, he let me go to the bathroom a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said you were put in cell number 3, if I remember correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was anybody else in that cell with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So you were there by yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Regarding the toilet, where was the cell in relation to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The toilet was, looking from the entrance to the left, and the cell was off to the left from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How far away from the toilet was your cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, four, five, six metres, I do not know. Several metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, according to your statement, it seems as if in this facility, you spent the time between 18th May through 19th June 1993. Was it always in the same cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was all in the same cell, with the exception of two or three days when Ivica Marus -- he was a Croat who was taken prisoner as he was a member of the BiH army, so we were put together in a cell. For a short period of time there was Muhamed and there were two people from Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So the entire time, with the exception of those two or three days, you were alone in the cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was alone in the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many cells, approximately, were there in this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many prisoners, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I was by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How often did you receive meals daily?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three times, but I did not eat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: During your stay in this facility, when was the first time you saw the accused, Zlatko Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When was it the first time that I saw him? When I arrived, when I came there and when I was told that the door was -- the door was open then and I was told to sing, "All the way to Fruska Gora". That is when I saw him first. I do not know if he was there with two or three other men to see me or not, but the first time officially I saw him when I asked to be taken to the doctors and when he took me there in his own car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How long after you were brought there was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We are talking about your being taken to the doctors.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how many days, to me the days were very long, so to me, it seemed very long. I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell at least approximately how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot, because I was being beaten every day, too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that when you first arrived you were told that you had to sing that song.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of a song it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am sure that the Trial Chamber does not know that, so could you please explain it to them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "All the way to Fruska Gora, there are Draza's guards and Pavelic's patrols." Pavelic was an Ustasha and Draza was a Chetnik, so that was the song.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Who sang these songs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I sang them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But they were not composed for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I had never heard it until I got there. I had never heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But from your schooling, you probably know who Draza Mihajlovic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know, I heard of him. He was a Chetnik, he was a Chetnik leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Who was Nikola Pavelic, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard he was some kind of an Ustasha leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know what were the relations between Chetniks and Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Were they allies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You did not learn about that in school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnic group the guards in the prison were of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To me it is a bit of a funny question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The Croats would be in a Muslim prison -- it may be funny to you, but not for the Trial Chamber, they need to know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Croats, one person from Zenica, he had thrown a hand grenade among the children and had to leave Zenica. Dragan Micic told me he was a Serb and wanted to go to America, but he was captured and he was trying to be good with them so that he would be let go, and for the rest I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, Dragan Micic was taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what he told me, he said, "I was captured and I was in a cell for a month, I went through that myself".

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I understand. You said that the warden Zlatko Aleksovski took you in his private car to the health centre in Busovaca to see the doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said, if I remember correctly, that you were alone, together with Aleksovski in the car, and that you sat in the back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and that Aleksovski told me, "do not try anything stupid, because if you try you will not succeed".

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that, you came to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You entered a building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, when I came out of the car, I was not able to get into the building and two nurses wanted to help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But the building did not come to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But we did not go into the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you find yourself in the building at some point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Where did you find yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We found ourselves in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, I am going to remind you that you said that you entered the building and you sat down in the waiting room; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct that we came in front of the building, that I could not get in, I fell down, the two nurses tried to help me and the gentleman -- I am not going to call him a gentleman, Aleksovski told them that they could not help me, I crawled in on all fours and came to the bench to sit down where the patients come and sit down to see a doctor. Then Aleksovski went in. I do not know what he said to them, but then at the next moment I was called into the doctor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that you were in the waiting room between ten and fifteen minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, I did not have a watch. Had I had a watch, they would have taken it away from me, but I did not have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did somebody guard you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody did, I think -- it was only one car that came here, I did not see anybody else. I do not know if they thought I would try something, but I did not see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, can you tell us, how come that you did not try to escape in such circumstances where nobody was watching you, and on the other hand you are jumping out of a moving car with four other persons there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I tried to jump, I was fit, I was able to do that, but when Aleksovski was taking me to the doctor's, I could not even take care of myself, let alone settle scores with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am not talking about settling scores, I am talking about you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not, I could not move.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After the visit to the doctor's, when you were coming back in the car, you said that you addressed Mr. Aleksovski, asking of him to arrange so that you would not be beaten any more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I pleaded with him not to beat me and to even cut my meals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But you did not ask what happened at the doctors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought we had settled that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the doctor asked me what was wrong with me, I said that I urinated -- that I had blood in urine and stool and Aleksovski interrupted me and said, "he only has a cold and he needs an injection". The doctor said I should strip to the waist so that she could check me and I was all black and blue and she said, "this is animal behaviour, he needs treatment". Aleksovski said, "we have it in prison, we have an infirmary, a special room for the sick". That was the same cell where I was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, do you not remember that you said this in these same words earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, who is Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know what position he held at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know at all. I knew later when I came out of the prison that he was a leader, that he had his own police force. Until then, I did not know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You did not know him from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him as a guest in coffee bars, not my own but other coffee bars, so we nodded to each other, but we did not talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What experiences did you have with Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In what sense?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because when Darko Kraljevic arrived, Mirko Selak and Brane Jukic, who wanted to take a statement of me, I was very badly beaten, together with six others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know somebody called Goran Medugorac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him from prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What does that mean, "from prison"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the camp, that is where I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In what capacity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the capacity of somebody who beat, because he beat me the worst.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What kind of position did he hold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How do you know his first and last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On several occasions, some people would say "Medugorac, you will kill him from beating", so several people called by that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The first name Goran, how did you know his name was Goran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because that is how they called him. He even had it tattooed on his forearm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at that time there was another person by the same last name in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, can you describe to us what kind of lock was on the door to your cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on the outside and inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was the door locked with a key?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with a key.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they asked of Dragan Micic to give them the key and he did not give them the key, so that is how I know it was locked with a key.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How do you know that he did not give it to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could hear it, you could hear it through this window, the barred window that we had there, so I could hear well if somebody knocked three times, I had to sing or if somebody in the corridor said, "for whom", I had to say, "for king and country".

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know whose slogan it is, "for king and country"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was the king in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard from my father when I was very small there was a king, that is all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Maybe from the school programme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Me and school, I was a poor student.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you hear when they would open the door to your cell that the door was actually unlocked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am perfectly aware of the fact that you cannot remember all the dates, but from the moment when you were arrested, how long were you imprisoned before the Red Cross arrived, or some other official organisation of that kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The International Red Cross only came once and that was 18 to 20 days later. I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to talk alone with the Red Cross representatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to talk to the Red Cross official at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did they identify you as a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received a paper, this is what I received from them, this is what I got (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is the card you got from them. What is written in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name and last name, my date of birth and residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How did they have this information if you did not tell them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I described that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else apart from the Red Cross representatives come to the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I mean specifically the European Monitors.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, I was all beaten up, I could not see, I could not look around. I was not able to look at people and see who they were, what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many days after the Red Cross visit were you set free?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twelve, ten, twelve, thirteen, I do not know exactly. For me it looked like 100 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That I believe you. Mr. Dautovic, you told us this morning that when the prisoners were released, their names were read out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At that time, you were in the cell, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And you heard your name read out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I banged the door with my fists, I screamed out as loudly as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And the door was opened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two men opened the door. One of them hit me immediately, but I had the greatest courage and strength to reach the Red Cross representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you were beaten when a woman from the Red Cross was standing about five or six metres away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was behind and I was in the cell. She was in the corridor and I was in the cell. The corridor is in the middle and the cells are on the left-hand side and right-hand side. I was on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you complain to that woman that you were hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not. I felt as if I had been born again, going from death to life.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was anyone else present, apart from that woman from the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were others, but I did not dare look. I just looked in front of myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When were you released, that is what time of day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think around midday. I think it was around midday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly whether it was 11.00 or 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think you said that you saw your name on the list written by hand, added by hand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was when I was entering the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you try to explain that to yourself in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. For me, all I cared about was to get going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So you got on to the bus and you were driven to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When did you reach Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In about an hour, I do not know exactly how long it takes for the bus to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And what happened when you arrived in Zenica, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We entered a building, they interrogated us, took pictures, recorded that I was beaten up, then we left that place, some people went home, I went to the hospital, I was driven to the hospital. I do not know who by, because when I realised that I could complain, that I could say how ill I was, then I was taken and put up in the hospital for treatment. I was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You were the only one out of all the 38?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Out of all the 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You were the 39th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When did you reach the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I was half conscious, I had kept my courage somehow up to then, but by then I had given up altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When did you leave the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, because the hospital was overcrowded. In the morning, I do not know whether it was 10.00 or 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Dautovic, were you able to walk then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Half able.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That means that I was not sure of myself, I could walk for about five metres and then I would stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What did you do after you left hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A man, a taxi driver had brought somebody to the hospital, I approached him, I introduced myself, I sat in his car and I told him immediately, "I have no money, can you take me home?". He said, "I cannot take you home because I do not have enough fuel. If you need money, here is some money, take another taxi. If you want me to take you up to some way" -- I said, "take me to the Gold restaurant in Zenica", because I was a good friend of the owner, so I went to that restaurant. I was filthy with a long beard, unwashed, smelly. Everybody was shocked, they thought I had gone mad. They bought me some coffee, they asked me what had happened. When I explained everything, they found a car and they drove me home. When I got home, they slaughtered a lamb, they put poultice with fresh meat on me and this went on for about two months, I was taken to the doctors regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What kind of treatment were you given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My family slaughtered a lamb and then the fresh skin of the lamb was bandaged round me to help heal the wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken, you said you ate very little in prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that when you went into prison, you were over 90 kilograms in weight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How much did you weigh when you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lost between 25 and 30 kilograms, I think, because maybe throughout that period I ate twice on the outside. I was given food but I could not eat, because I was beaten all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, on 18th May 1993 when you were arrested, were hostilities still going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they had not started. A day before that, I went to Novi Travnik, I had the courage to go wherever I wanted to. Before that I went to Novi Travnik, and I was captured by the HVO. They shut me up, they kept me there for three days and afterwards they let me go. When they had questioned me, when they saw that I was not in politics, they let me go and nobody touched me until Aleksovski got hold of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But it was not Aleksovski who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not, but I was brought to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said this morning, Mr. Dautovic, that you still have problems as a consequence of this to this day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, considerable problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I understood properly, these are problems mostly of a psychiatric nature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What kind of medication are you taking? You said you were taking something, so I am asking you what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am talking maurines and some other medicines. Then they give me sleeping pills because I suffer terribly from insomnia and forgetfulness also, loss of memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, what you have described that happened to you happened more than four years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: During that four-year period, did you talk about what happened to you with someone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I started talking to some people, I did, but I avoided it, because this was very painful, so I avoided it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you make any official statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us when and to whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I made a statement in Zenica, in the security service centre in the district court, and last year also in the security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell the Trial Chamber what CSB is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what kind of police that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But the Trial Chamber does not know what a MUP is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you ever make a statement for the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Are you sure of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am, but only when we left they were recording. When we came out of the camp, they taped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Zenica. I do not know where it was, but I did not specially go to make a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So in Zenica you were recorded, when you reached Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a microphone going round. I do not even know what it was about, I heard from other people that there were reports in the press of what I said, but I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the statement that you made on that occasion in Zenica now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, you said that you have the same coffee bar today, fortunately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a coffee bar in my own house, but it is in another house, because I have two houses now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How much are you making today, roughly, per month.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have just closed the bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How much did you make last month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not been working for some time, the whole past year maybe for two months only, because there is no business left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What are you living off? Are you employed, are you working anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you have some savings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had some savings and my sister's son is in Germany so he sends me some money. I have a sister in Zagreb and she sends me some money too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So you are not making any money yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your car I think you said you never saw it again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That one no, but I have another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, thank you for your testimony, and I hope you will recover well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hardly expect that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, a couple of questions more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No problems, as many as you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Dragica Viskovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Ante Puselj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know Ante Puselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who he is? Is he a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was my neighbour and friend and he is a dear friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And a person called Ivica Marus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him in the camp, when that monodrama took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You mean what you described to us this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, my last question, I will not bother you any more. I want to show you a list, so could you please tell us whether you know some people from that list. Could the usher please show the witness a list of persons detained in Kaonik that has been admitted into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit, I think P7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read rather slowly. (Pause). I cannot see anything like that. I cannot see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, will you look at the paper? It will be easier for you than to read it from the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You do not know a single person on this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anyone. MR.. MIKULICIC: The Defence has no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your Honour, just two questions to clarify one matter in re-examination. Mr. Dautovic, you said to this court in cross-examination, as well as in the examination-in-chief, that you went to Guca Gora to buy cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Those cigarettes were to be sold in your restaurant in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the restaurant or outside the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You wanted to make as much profit as possible from the sale of those cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if I had managed to sell them, I might have gone back to Guca Gora again the next day, because he told me he would have more cigarettes the next day. MR.. MEDDEGODA: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic, you have completed your testimony. We wish to thank you for coming. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I think you would like to take the floor, Mr. Prosecutor? I was about to suggest that we have the break before bringing in the next witness. MR.. MEDDEGODA: Very good, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If you wish. MR.. MEDDEGODA: As it please your Honours, we will take the break at this stage and call the witness afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well. Then we can have a break until 4.05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor? MR.. MEDDEGODA: Your Honours, the Prosecution would call witness Vahid Hajdarevic. VAHID HAJDAREVIC (sworn)

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you please give your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vahid Hajdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 3rd December 1965.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Please tell this court where you were born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Busovaca, in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity, Mr. Hajdarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Muslim, a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And your religion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand, I am a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your religion would be Islam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Islam.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Prior to 1993, you lived in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were you employed at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a building construction enterprise called Nisko Gradna Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: For how long were you employed in that company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think for about three years, because before that, I worked in Medjapan and Vatro Stelna, also in Busovaca, but the last company I worked for was Nisko Gradna.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Until when were you employed in Nisko Gradna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the outbreak of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and my work booklet is still in that same enterprise, so that my labour relationship has not been broken off.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: At any point in time were you mobilised into the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 16th April 1992, when the aggression was carried out against Bosnia-Herzegovina by Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: After you were mobilised, did you at any point in time have to serve in any part of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in Busovaca. At that time, because the Serbian Chetnik aggressor was attacking certain parts of the municipalities of Iljos and Visoko. As a member of the Territorial Defence, I was deployed on the front-line for some 15 days in June, then in September and then again in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What was the situation like in Busovaca by about December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is rather difficult to explain that situation in brief, but I shall try and be as concise as possible. Members of the Territorial Defence wanted to defend the integrity of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereas the HVO members at that time were always within certain armed forces, but they focused more on obstructing the work of the government in Busovaca itself and were trying to place the town in a blockade. I do not know whether that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: When they tried to place the town in a blockade, what happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Various incidents occurred, starting from mistreatment and harassment, disarming of members of the TO, and even plundering and looting of some resources. For instance, I know that some vehicles from us that were going for Slovenia were confiscated by the HVO, so all kinds of looting and plunder occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you tell this court when the incidents began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around October, I think. Even before that, there were some minor incidents, but these were resolved by negotiation. But as from October, as far as I can recall, they took over a number of institutions in the municipality, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR.. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you tell us who took over -- you said "a number of institutions in the municipality", and the police were taken over; who took over those institutions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
